Let $(S,m)$ be a finite Coxeter matrix; let $W$ and $\ell$ be the presented group and its length and let $\sigma:W\to\mathrm{GL}_K(E)$ be the geometric representation, as in [[def-hh-coxeter-matrix-word-group-and-length]], [[def-hh-geometric-coxeter-representation-and-roots]] and [[lem-hh-dihedral-root-recurrence-and-root-sign]], with reflection set $T$ and sign-change sets $\Phi(w)$ as in that lemma. Parts (1) and (2) hold for every finite $S$, including the empty and singleton cases; a distinct pair is required only for part (3).

1. **Braid moves.** Call two words in $S$ *braid-equivalent* when one is obtained from the other by finitely many replacements of an alternating subword $s\,t\,s\,t\cdots$ of length $m(s,t)<\infty$ by the alternating word $t\,s\,t\,s\cdots$ of the same length. Then any two reduced expressions of the same element $w\in W$ are braid-equivalent.
2. **M-reducedness.** A word is reduced if and only if no sequence of braid moves followed by cancellation of a consecutive equal pair can shorten it (M-reduced in the sense of [Davis, Definition 3.4.1]).
3. **Singleton detection in dihedral subgroups.** Fix distinct $s,t\in S$ and put $m:=m(s,t)$. The subgroup $\langle s,t\rangle\le W$ is dihedral of order $2m$ when $m<\infty$ and infinite dihedral when $m=\infty$; every element of $\langle s,t\rangle$ acts on the quotient $E/\operatorname{span}(\alpha_s,\alpha_t)$ as the identity, while for every $u\in S\setminus\{s,t\}$ one has $\sigma_u(\alpha_u)-\alpha_u=-2\alpha_u\notin\operatorname{span}(\alpha_s,\alpha_t)$ (no induced quotient map for $\sigma_u$ is assumed). ([[def-graded-ring-module-bimodule-and-internal-shift]]). The category
$\operatorname{GrMod}_0(A)$ of graded left $A$-modules and degree-zero maps is
abelian ([[lem-graded-module-kernels-cokernels-and-biproducts-are-degreewise]]).

**Graded projective.** $P$ is **graded projective** when it is a projective
object of $\operatorname{GrMod}_0(A)$ ([[def-projective-object]]): for every
degree-zero epimorphism $q:E\twoheadrightarrow M$ and every degree-zero
$f:P\to M$ there exists a degree-zero $\widetilde f:P\to E$ with
$q\widetilde f=f$. Thus projectivity is tested only against degree-zero
epimorphisms and degree-zero maps, and the lift need not be unique.

**Finitely generated.** $P$ is **finitely generated as a graded left
$A$-module**, or generated by finitely many homogeneous elements, when for some
$n\ge0$ there are homogeneous elements $p_1,\dots,p_n\in P$ with

$$P=A p_1+\cdots+A p_n .$$

By [[def-generated-cyclic-finitely-generated-and-free-modules]] this is the same
notion as finite generation of the underlying $A$-module: a finite homogeneous
family is a finite family, and conversely, if $P=\langle S\rangle_A$ for a
finite set $S$, then writing each $s=\sum_es_e$ as its finite sum of nonzero
homogeneous components gives, for every $x=\sum_{s\in S}a_s s\in P$,

$$x=\sum_{s\in S}a_s\sum_es_e=\sum_{s,e}a_s s_e,$$

a finite $A$-linear combination of the homogeneous elements $s_e\in P$; so the
finitely many components of the members of $S$ generate $P$. In particular the
notion does not depend on the chosen finite generating set.

**Finite graded projective.** $P$ is **finite graded projective** when it is
graded projective and generated by finitely many homogeneous elements, that is,
when it is graded projective and finitely generated as an $A$-module. The family
may be empty: $n=0$ gives $P=Ap_1+\cdots+Ap_n=0$, so the zero module is
generated by the empty homogeneous family, and the corresponding finite direct
sum of shifts in the characterization below is the empty direct sum. Its finite
shifted-free characterization is the next result
([[thm-finite-graded-projectives-are-summands-of-finite-graded-free-modules]]),
and it uses this same notion of finite generation throughout: a finite
homogeneous generating family there is exactly a family as above. No choice
principle is used in the equivalence above, which only rewrites a given finite
expression.

nonzero finite-dimensional graded left $A$-module whose only graded submodules

Let $C_\beta$ be the color-symmetric polynomial subalgebra: on the summand $e(\nu)R(\beta)e(\nu)$ it is the polynomial ring in the elementary symmetric functions of the dots of each color separately. It is central: unequal crossings permute dot positions, and equal-color divided differences $\partial_a$ commute with symmetric polynomials in $x_a,x_{a+1}$ by the Leibniz rule $\partial_a(fg)=\partial_a(f)g+s_a(f)\partial_a(g)$ applied to $s_a$-invariant $f$. In each constant-color block of length $m$ the polynomial ring $k[x_1,\dots,x_m]$ is free over the symmetric subring on the Artin monomials $x_1^{a_1}\cdots x_m^{a_m}$, $0\le a_r\le m-r$: adjoining the first root of the universal polynomial $T^m-e_1T^{m-1}+\cdots+(-1)^me_m$ presents $k[x_1,\dots,x_m]$ as a free rank-$m$ module over the coefficient ring, the corresponding quotient of $T^m-\cdots$ by $T-x_1$ is monic of degree $m-1$ with the correct coefficients, and iteration gives those monomials as a basis while the elementary symmetric functions of the roots recover the $e_r$. Combining with the PBW basis [F1], whose dot monomials factor over the color blocks, gives that $R(\beta)$ is a finite free $C_\beta$-module, of rank $(|\beta|!)^2$ per weight counting the permutation basis; only centrality and this freeness are used below.

(Krull-Schmidt and splitting.) Every finitely generated graded module is bounded below and locally finite by [F1]. Choose finitely many homogeneous generators of degrees $d_j$; evaluation on the generators injects $\operatorname{End}^0(M)$ into the finite product of the finitely many finite-dimensional pieces $M_{d_j}$, so every degree-zero endomorphism algebra is finite-dimensional, and a nontrivial homogeneous idempotent splits $M$ into two nonzero summands with strictly smaller endomorphism algebras; splitting terminates. For an indecomposable $M$, every endomorphism $f$ satisfies a polynomial minimal equation because $\operatorname{End}^0(M)$ is finite-dimensional; factoring it as $T^rg(T)$ with $g(0)\ne0$, Bezout gives a polynomial projector separating the nilpotent part from the invertible part, so indecomposability forces $f$ or $1-f$ to be invertible. Hence the nonunits form the unique maximal ideal, and the usual comparison of two decompositions $\bigoplus p_ii_jp_j=\mathrm{id}$ produces a matching summand and cancellation, proving uniqueness in the degree-zero category; the shifts are recorded as part of each summand.

(Simples and covers.) below, and it introduces no sign.

**Outer actions.** If $M$ is a graded $(B,A)$-bimodule and $N$ a graded left
$A$-module, then the action $b(m\otimes n):=(bm)\otimes n$ of
[[thm-bimodule-actions-induced-on-tensor-products]] makes $M\otimes_AN$ a graded
left $B$-module: the action is homogeneous because homogeneous $b\in B_l$ sends
$m\otimes n$ of degree $i+j$ to an element of degree $l+i+j$. Symmetrically, if
$N$ is a graded $(A,C)$-bimodule, the action
$(m\otimes n)c:=m\otimes(nc)$ makes $M\otimes_AN$ a graded right $C$-module, and
the two outer actions commute when both are present.

derivations.claim: (Shuffle decomposition and freeness.) Choose reduced PBW words adapted to the parabolic subgroup $S_{|\beta|}\times S_{|\gamma|}$. For each concatenated word $\xi=\nu\ast\eta$ and minimal right coset representative $w$, the vectors $\tau_we(\xi)b$, with $b$ ranging through the PBW basis of $e(\xi)B$, form precisely the PBW basis of the right $B$-module $Ae$: the permutation is a minimal shuffle followed by an internal block permutation, with additive length, and the right idempotent records the source word in the corner $e$. Thus $Ae\cong\bigoplus_{w,\xi}e(\xi)B\{\delta_R(w,\xi)\}$, with the displayed degree of $\tau_we(\xi)$. Reversal of products fixing dots, crossings and idempotents preserves the defining relations and is an anti-involution; it sends $Ae$ to $eA$ and $\tau_we(\xi)$ to $e(\xi)\tau_{w^{-1}}$, giving the left $B$-module decomposition of $eA$ into the corresponding $Be(\xi)$ with shifts $\delta_L(w,\xi)=\deg(e(\xi)\tau_w)$. Both decompositions are finite sums of principal graded projectives. Ungraded, for each shuffle the sum over all concatenated $\xi$ is one copy of $B$, so both ranks are $\binom{|\beta|+|\gamma|}{|\beta|}$. Neither bimodule is replaced by $eAe$: its unconstrained opposite endpoint is essential for the shuffle basis.

(Left adjunction.) For a graded left $B$-module $X$ and a graded left $A$-module $L$, currying gives the natural degree-zero bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{A,0}(Ae\otimes_BX,L)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{B,0}(X,eL)$, $\Phi\mapsto(x\mapsto\Phi(e\otimes x))$, with inverse $f\mapsto(ae\otimes x\mapsto a\,f(x))$, well defined on balanced tensors and inverse by the idempotence of $e$; this is the adjunction of [F3] for the $(A,B)$-bimodule $Ae$.

(Exactness and projectivity.) The right $B$-module $Ae$ is projective, hence flat, by step 1.1, so $\mathrm{Ind}=Ae\otimes_B-$ is exact by [F2]. Idempotent restriction is exact on left modules: for a surjection $L\to N$, a vector $en\in eN$ lifts to $e\ell\in eL$, and kernels and images commute with multiplication by the degree-zero idempotent $e$; no right action on $L$ is required. A finitely generated graded projective left $B$-module is a summand of a finite sum of shifts of $B$, so its induction is a summand of the corresponding sum of shifts of $Ae$. As a left $A$-module $Ae$ is the image of the degree-zero idempotent endomorphism $a\mapsto ae$ of $A$, hence is finitely generated graded projective. Similarly, if $P$ is a finitely generated graded projective left $A$-module, realize $P$ as a summand of a finite sum of shifts of $A$ and apply $e(-)$ to its split inclusion and projection. Then $eP$ is a summand of the corresponding sum of shifts of $eA$, which is finitely generated graded projective as a left $B$-module by step 1.1. Internal shifts commute with induction and restriction because their balance relations and idempotent action have degree zero. This proves exactness, shift compatibility and both finite-projective preservation clauses.

(Coinduction and the longest shuffle.) The right adjoint of $\mathrm{Res}$ is $\mathrm{Coind}=\operatorname{HOM}_B(eA,-)$ by [F3] applied to $M=eA$, and explicit currying gives $(a\cdot f)(t)=f(ta)$. For the second-adjunction formula let $y$ be the longest block shuffle of the two blocks, of degree $-c$ (each of the $|\beta||\gamma|$ crossed positions contributes the negative pairing of the two colours), and let $e'=e(\gamma,\beta)$ be the reversed-block idempotent. By PBW there is a well-defined $B$-balanced coefficient map $t:eAe'\to B$ projecting onto the $y$-coefficient, where the reversed block order is read in $B$ through the flip equivalence $R(\beta)\otimes_kR(\gamma)\to R(\gamma)\otimes_kR(\beta)$; dot slides and block crossings preserve the longest-shuffle coefficient, while every dot or braid correction in a shorter shuffle has strictly smaller shuffle length and is killed by $t$. Hence the map $\Phi:Ae'\to\operatorname{HOM}_B(eA,B)$, $z\mapsto(u\mapsto t(uz))$, is a degree-$c$ map of $(A,B)$-bimodules, and it is compatible with the flip identification.

(Mackey filtration.) Fix a second flag with idempotent $e'=e(\beta',\gamma')$ and choose reduced double-coset representatives for the row block permutation group and the column block permutation group acting on the $|\beta|+|\gamma|$ positions. Partition the PBW monomials of the corner $eAe'$ by the four intersection blocks $(a,b;c,d)$ with row sums $\beta,\gamma$ and column sums $\beta',\gamma'$, and filter by the crossing length of the double-coset representatives. The span of the double cosets of strictly smaller length is a $(B,B')$-sub-bimodule: sliding a block generator across a representative either stays in its double coset with an internal block permutation, or produces a quadratic/braid correction of strictly smaller length, which lies in the smaller span. In the associated quotient only the monomials whose permutation is the minimal double-coset representative survive; they are exactly tensor products of the PBW bases of the four blocks composed with the row and column induced bimodules and the unique minimal crossing of the two middle blocks, which carries the shift $-(b\mid c)$ because the crossed colours are precisely $b$ and $c$. The basis bijection defines inverse maps between the associated quotient and the composite four-block restriction/induction bimodule, so the filtration is proved and not merely a character identity; iterating the same permutation argument gives the multi-block statement.

(Triangularity and the functor formula.) Pair the right $B$-module shuffle basis of $Ae'$ (through the block flip) with the left $B$-module shuffle basis of $eA$ by complementary shuffles. Ordered by shuffle length, the coefficient matrix of the pairing $u\mapsto t(uz)$ is triangular: a complementary pair is exactly the reduced longest shuffle with coefficient $1$ up to the absorbed equal-colour signs, and a noncomplementary pair either misses its permutation or reduces by a quadratic or braid correction to strictly smaller length, hence vanishes in the associated graded. $$T_{i,c,t}:=\begin{bmatrix}K_i;c\\ t\end{bmatrix}:=\prod_{s=1}^{t}\frac{K_iq_i^{\,c-s+1}-K_i^{-1}q_i^{\,-c+s-1}}{q_i^{\,s}-q_i^{\,-s}}\in U_q(\mathfrak g),$$

the empty product being $T_{i,c,0}:=1$. Each factor is defined in
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ because $q_i^{\,s}-q_i^{\,-s}\ne0$ for $s\ge1$
([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]), so
$T_{i,c,t}$ is a polynomial in $K_i^{\pm1}$ with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$;
in particular all $T_{i,c,t}$ commute with the $K_h$ and with one another
(Verification, step 2.1).

The **Lusztig divided-power integral form** is the $A$-subalgebra

$$U_A:=\bigl\langle E_i^{(r)},\ F_i^{(r)},\ K_h^{\pm1},\ T_{i,c,t}\ \colon\ i\in I,\ r,t\ge0,\ c\in\mathbb Z,\ h\in P^{\vee}\bigr\rangle\ \subseteq\ U_q(\mathfrak g),$$

where $x^{(r)}=x^r/[r]_i!$ are the divided powers of
[[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. Write $U_A^\pm$
for the $A$-subalgebras generated by the $E_i^{(r)}$ and by the $F_i^{(r)}$,
and $U_A^0$ for the one generated by the $K_h^{\pm1}$ and the $T_{i,c,t}$.

Then:

(i) $U_A$ contains $E_i=E_i^{(1)}$, $F_i=F_i^{(1)}$ and all $K_h$;

(ii) $U_A$ is a root-graded $A$-subalgebra of the root-graded
$\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ ([[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]):
with $U_A[\beta]:=U_A\cap U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$ one has
$U_A=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q}U_A[\beta]$, each $U_A[\beta]$ is an $A$-submodule,
and $U_A^\pm,U_A^0$ are graded in the same way;

(iii) $U_A\otimes_A\mathbb Q(q)\cong U_q(\mathfrak g)$ canonically, i.e. the
$\mathbb Q(q)$-span of $U_A$ is all of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$.

The shifted binomials $T_{i,c,t}$ with $c\ne0$ are included because the
divided-power reordering identity of
[[lem-divided-power-and-toral-quantum-binomial-reordering-identities]] has
coefficients $T_{i,2t-a-b,t}$ with a nonconstant index; the specializations at
$q=1$ of these elements are computed in
[[lem-q-one-toral-specialization-identifies-the-classical-cartan-generators]],
and the integral triangular decomposition and the specialization are treated
only after this definition.

No freeness of $U_A$ or of its parts over $A$, no independence of the listed
generators, and no triangularity of the products of the three parts is asserted
here. In particular $A$ is not a principal ideal domain (Verification, step
7.1), so no torsion-free-to-free inference over $A$ is permitted anywhere on
this page.

Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra of a finite symmetrizable Cartan datum, over $k=\mathbb Q(q)$, and let $U_q^-,U_q^0,U_q^+$ be its generated subalgebras of [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]].

(i) Multiplication is a vector-space isomorphism
$$m:U_q^-\otimes_k U_q^0\otimes_k U_q^+\longrightarrow U_q(\mathfrak g),\qquad x_-\otimes x_0\otimes x_+\longmapsto x_-x_0x_+.$$
Products $b_-K_h b_+$, with $b_\pm$ ranging over supplied bases of the two halves and $h\in P^\vee$, form a basis of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$. Arbitrary simple-generator words span the halves; their Serre relations preclude claiming their independence.

(ii) The halves are exactly the algebras presented by their separate Serre relations, and $U_q^0\cong k[P^\vee]$. Thus all three abstract factor maps are injective and the $K_h$ are linearly independent.

(iii) For every $\beta\in Q$, the total root grading satisfies
$$U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]\cong\bigoplus_{\alpha,\gamma\in Q_+,\,\alpha-\gamma=\beta} U_q^-[-\gamma]\otimes_k U_q^0\otimes_k U_q^+[\alpha].$$
In particular degree zero contains all equal-positive/negative-degree summands, including $F_iE_i$; it is not just the toral subalgebra. As a left $U_q^0$-module this component is free, with rank equal to the possibly infinite sum of the products of the two half-component dimensions. Under AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the half-component dimensions are their classical PBW ranks, and products of the generic PBW bases of [[thm-generic-quantum-serre-halves-have-classical-pbw-ranks-and-a-nondegenerate-hopf-pairing]] with the toral basis give a PBW basis of the whole algebra. AC enters only through that supplier's formal-embedding proof; (i), (ii) and the graded tensor decomposition are choice-free.

derivations.claim: (Induction algebra and restriction coalgebra.) The induction product is associative and unital: the balanced identifications of [[def-klr-induction-and-restriction-bimodules]] for the two parenthesizations of three blocks are inverse degree-zero isomorphisms, and the unit is $[R(0)]=[k]$. For the block algebra $B$, the positive-center quotient is the tensor product of the two finite-dimensional graded quotients from [[lem-klr-module-categories-are-krull-schmidt-with-shift-orbit-bases]]. Their simples are absolutely simple by [[lem-klr-maximal-tail-restriction-and-induction-have-a-unique-simple-head]], so their graded semisimple quotients are products of split graded matrix algebras. Tensoring these matrix blocks gives all simple shift orbits of $B$; tensor products of the factor projective covers cover them, by reducing their kernels and using the graded least-degree argument. Uniqueness of covers therefore identifies $K_0(B)$ with $K_0(R(\beta))\otimes_AK_0(R(\gamma))$. Restriction is coassociative with counit the weight-zero component, because iterated idempotent restriction multiplies the corresponding block idempotents, and the two orders of multiplication agree. To prove that $[\mathrm{Res}]$ respects the twisted multiplication, apply the Mackey filtration [F1] to the corner $e_{\beta,\gamma}Re_{\beta',\gamma'}$: PBW partitions its basis by the double cosets of the two block permutation groups, ordered by crossing length, and multiplication across a braid move changes only smaller-length terms; the associated quotient is exactly the four-block restriction/induction bimodule shifted by minus the root pairing of the two crossed middle blocks. Taking classes gives $[\mathrm{Res}](xy)=\sum q^{-(|y_2|\mid|x_1'|)}x_1x_1'\otimes x_2x_2'$ with the twisted product, so $[\mathrm{Res}]$ is an algebra homomorphism; no use of the second adjunction is needed.

(Explicit Serre contraction.) Fix $i\ne j$, write $d=-a_{ij}$, $D=d+1$, $N=d+2$, and $t=[u^d]Q_{ij}\ne0$. For $0\le r\le D$, let $E_r$ be the product of the reflected nil-Hecke idempotents on the two $i$-blocks in $i^rji^{D-r}$, let $s_r=-d_i(\binom r2+\binom{D-r}2)$, and put $C_r=R E_r\{s_r\}$. Use right multiplication by $a_r=E_r\tau_{N-1}\cdots\tau_{r+1}E_{r+1}$ for $C_r\to C_{r+1}$ and by $b_r=E_{r+1}\tau_1\cdots\tau_{r+1}E_r$ in the reverse direction. Each string crosses $j$ once and respectively $D-r-1$ or $r$ equal-color pairs, so its degrees are $d_id-2d_i(D-r-1)$ and $d_id-2d_ir$. As $s_{r+1}-s_r=d_i(D-2r-1)$, both maps have degree zero between the shifted columns. The nil-Hecke identities $\tau_aE_r=0$ for equal-color crossings internal to its divided blocks and the braid moves give $a_{r-1}a_r=0$. At corner $r$, put $L_r=a_rb_r$, $R_r=b_{r-1}a_{r-1}$, with absent endpoint terms zero. Moving far crossings cancels the common strings in $L_r-R_r$; the remaining braid correction is the divided difference of $Q_{ij}$. For a monomial $u^av^b$ its correction is the sum of $a$ monomials of combined outer degree $a-1$, with the native minus sign. The $r-1$ left and $D-r-1$ right equal-color divided differences kill it unless $a\ge d$; homogeneity permits $a=d$ only when $b=0$, and permits no $a>d$. For $a=d$ exactly the staircase exponents $r-1,D-r-1$ survive, each evaluated by the nil-Hecke trace calculation of [[def-divided-power-klr-idempotents-and-projectives]]; transporting the variable order on the left block gives $L_r-R_r=(-1)^rtE_r$, including endpoints. Thus $h_r=(-1)^rt^{-1}b_r$ satisfies $a_rh_r+h_{r-1}a_{r-1}=E_r$ on every corner. These degree-zero maps contract the finite complex $(C_r,a_r)$ over every field and every (Q1)–(Q4) parameter.

(Alternating classes and the $a_{ij}=0$ case.) A bounded complex with $dh+hd=1$ is split contractible: choosing the successive splittings gives a contraction with $h^2=0$, and then $d+h$ is an isomorphism from even to odd part; hence the alternating sum of the classes of its terms vanishes, which is exactly $\sum_{a+b=D}(-1)^a[P_{i,a}][P_{j,1}][P_{i,b}]=0$, the displayed Serre relation. If $a_{ij}=0$ then the crossing $\tau$ of the two colours is invertible (its square is the nonzero constant $Q_{ij}$), and right multiplication by it gives a degree-zero isomorphism between the two corners, so $[P_{i,1}][P_{j,1}]=[P_{ij}]=[P_{ji}]=[P_{j,1}][P_{i,1}]$.

(Descent of $\gamma$.) First define $\gamma$ over $\mathbb Q(q)$ from the presentation of the negative Serre half: [F3] identifies the Serre-presented rational negative half with the actual negative subalgebra, and the assignments $\theta_i\mapsto[P_{i,1}]$, extended multiplicatively and $q$-linearly, respect all Serre relations by step 3.1 and the commuting relation, so they define an algebra homomorphism $\gamma_{\mathbb Q}$ on the localization. Since the $A$-form is the $A$-subalgebra spanned by ordered divided words [F2], and $[P_{i,1}]^n=[n]_i![P_{i,n}]$ by the nil-Hecke decomposition, so every rational divided power maps to $[P_{i,n}]$. These divided-word images lie in $K_0(R)$, which embeds in its rational scalar extension because its shift-orbit basis is free, the homomorphism restricts to the stated $A$-linear $\gamma$; the formula $\gamma(\theta_{i_1}^{(n_1)}\cdots\theta_{i_r}^{(n_r)})=[\mathrm{Ind}(P_{i_1,n_1}\boxtimes\cdots\boxtimes P_{i_r,n_r})]$ is multiplicativity of $\gamma$ together with the definition of $P_\theta$. Coproduct compatibility is the Mackey computation of step 1.1, and bar compatibility is the projective $^\#$ duality of [[def-divided-power-klr-idempotents-and-projectives]], which fixes each normalized $P_{i,n}$ and hence each word class. No source parameter-specialization is asserted to preserve projective ranks.

For $\beta\in Q_+$ define the **Cartan pairing**
$$([P],[Q])_\beta:=\mathrm{gdim}_k\bigl(P^{\psi}\otimes_{R(\beta)}Q\bigr)\in\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\cdot(\beta)_q,\qquad (\beta)_q:=\prod_i\prod_{a=1}^{\beta_i}\frac1{1-q^{2d_i a}},$$
for finitely generated graded projective modules $P,Q$, where $\mathrm{gdim}_kM=\sum_{m\in\mathbb Z}q^m\dim_kM_m$; the tensor is over the graded algebra with the total-degree grading ([[def-graded-balanced-tensor-product-and-homogeneous-hom]]). Equivalently define the **hom pairing** $([P],[Q])'_\beta:=\mathrm{gdim}_k\operatorname{HOM}_{R(\beta)}(P,Q)$ ([[def-projective-simple-hom-pairing-on-grothendieck-groups]], [[thm-projective-hom-pairing-is-additive-and-graded-sesquilinear]]); then $([P],[Q])'_\beta=([P^\#],[Q])_\beta$ for the graded left projective $P^\#:=\operatorname{HOM}_{R(\beta)}(P,R(\beta))^\psi$. Thus the tensor form is symmetric and bilinear; the Hom form is conjugate-linear in its first variable and linear in its second. For the tensor form $([P],q[Q])=q([P],[Q])$ and $(q[P],[Q])=q([P],[Q])$, while the Hom form obeys $h(q^r[P],q^s[Q])=q^{s-r}h([P],[Q])$. [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]), and let

normalization**

(C) $B(1,Q)=\varepsilon(Q)$ for all $Q\in U_q^-$,

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum and let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra of [[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], with $q_i=q^{d_i}$, $K_i:=K_{d_ih_i}$, coproduct $\Delta$, counit $\varepsilon$ and antipode $S$ as in [[thm-the-drinfeld-jimbo-formulas-define-a-hopf-algebra]]. On the source side take Lusztig's presentation over $\mathbb Q(v)$, where $v$ is an indeterminate and $v_i=v^{d_i}$; the transport below sends $v_i$ to $q_i^{-1}$: generators $E_i^{L},F_i^{L},K_h^{L}$, the toral relations $K_h^{L}K_{h'}^{L}=K_{h+h'}^{L}$, $K_0^{L}=1$, the toral-action relations
$$K_h^{L}E_i^{L}=v^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}E_i^{L}K_h^{L},\qquad K_h^{L}F_i^{L}=v^{-\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}F_i^{L}K_h^{L},$$
the mixed relations $E_i^{L}F_j^{L}-F_j^{L}E_i^{L}=\delta_{ij}(K_i^{L}-(K_i^{L})^{-1})/(v_i-v_i^{-1})$, and the Serre relations with $v_i$-Gaussian binomial coefficients; let $\Delta_L$ be the source coproduct on generators
$$\Delta_L E_i^{L}=E_i^{L}\otimes1+K_i^{L}\otimes E_i^{L},\qquad \Delta_L F_i^{L}=F_i^{L}\otimes(K_i^{L})^{-1}+1\otimes F_i^{L},\qquad \Delta_L K_h^{L}=K_h^{L}\otimes K_h^{L}.$$
Let $B_K$ be the normalized Kashiwara half form on $U_q^-$ of [[thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral]], with skew derivations $e_i',e_i''$ of [[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]], and let $\psi$ be the bar involution of [[lem-the-lusztig-integral-form-is-stable-under-bar-and-contravariant-duality]]. Then:

(i) **Parameter transport.** The assignment $\varphi(v)=q^{-1}$, $\varphi(E_i^L)=E_i$, $\varphi(F_i^L)=F_i$, $\varphi(K_h^L)=K_{-h}$ defines an algebra isomorphism semilinear for the field isomorphism $\mathbb Q(v)\to\mathbb Q(q)$, $v\mapsto q^{-1}$. Its inverse sends $q\mapsto v^{-1}$ and $K_h\mapsto K_{-h}^L$, fixing the root generators. After the separate coefficient-renaming isomorphism $\rho:v\mapsto q$, $K_h^L\mapsto K_h$, this transport is $\varphi=\psi\rho$, with $\psi$ the library bar involution. It carries the source integral form onto $U_A$, fixes divided powers, inverts toral generators and fixes $T_{i,c,t}$. One must not apply the library bar a second time to the already transported parameter $v=q^{-1}$.

(ii) **Coproduct transport.** On all of the source algebra, $(\varphi\otimes\varphi)\circ\Delta_L=\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\circ\varphi$, where $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}=\mathrm{flip}\circ\Delta$. Equivalently the source coproduct is the opposite of the fixed library coproduct after parameter transport: the flip of the transported source coproduct is $\Delta$. In particular, with the barred coproduct $\bar\Delta(u):=(\psi\otimes\psi)\Delta(\psi(u))$, an element of the completed tensor square satisfying the source intertwining convention for $\Delta_L$ has a transport-flip that satisfies the library convention $\Delta(u)\Theta=\Theta\bar\Delta(u)$; this is the convention under which the normalized family of (vi) is read.

(iii) **The abstract half and its twisted product.** Transporting $\theta_i\mapsto F_i$ sends the source half $\mathbf f$ to $U_q^-$, the divided powers $\theta_i^{(n)}$ to $F_i^{(n)}$, and the source twisted coproduct multiplication $(x_1\otimes x_2)(y_1\otimes y_2)=v^{\langle\deg x_2,\deg y_1\rangle}x_1y_1\otimes x_2y_2$ to
$$(x_1\otimes x_2)(y_1\otimes y_2)=q^{-\langle\deg x_2,\deg y_1\rangle}x_1y_1\otimes x_2y_2$$
on $U_q^-\otimes U_q^-$; the coefficient extraction $e_i'(F_jQ)=\delta_{ij}Q+q_i^{-a_{ij}}F_je_i'(Q)$ of the transported twisted coproduct agrees with the library skew derivation $e_i'$.

(iv) **The half form up to the root-color factor.** On the homogeneous degree $\nu=\sum_i\nu_i\alpha_i$ the source form and the normalized Kashiwara form are related by
$$B_L=C_\nu\,B_K,\qquad C_\nu=\prod_i(1-q_i^2)^{-\nu_i},$$
a color-degree scaling which is a unit congruent to $1$ modulo $q$ and is not a single scalar on the whole half; for $P,Q$ of different degrees both sides vanish. In the rank-one subalgebra $B_L(F_i^{(n)},F_i^{(n)})=\prod_{r=1}^n(1-q_i^{2r})^{-1}$.

(v) **The normalized Drinfeld pairing.** Let $\iota:U_q^+\to U_q^-$ be the algebra isomorphism $E_i\mapsto F_i$. On homogeneous elements of opposite degrees set
$$D(x,y)=d_\nu^{-1}B_K(\iota x,y),\qquad d_\nu=\prod_i(q_i-q_i^{-1})^{\nu_i}\ \ (\deg x=\nu,\ \deg y=-\nu),$$
and set $D(x,y)=0$ for degrees not opposite. Then $D$ is a well-defined homogeneous pairing, perfect on every finite graded piece, and $D(E_i,F_j)=\delta_{ij}/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$; the pairing with generator value $1$ is the $B_K$-transport $B_K(\iota x,y)$. Its divided-power values are
$$D(E_i^{(n)},F_i^{(n)})=\frac{q_i^{-n(n-1)/2}}{[n]_i!\,(q_i-q_i^{-1})^n}.$$

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.
